html:
The fifth ecumenical council of the church, called by Justinian and held in Constantinople from May to June 553. Almost all the bishops were from the east.

Justinian wanted to win back the many Christians in Egypt and Syria who rejected the Council of Chalcedon, the Miaphysites. To please them, the council condemned the "Three Chapters": the writings of three earlier theologians thought to lean toward Nestorius. It also condemned ideas linked to Origen.

Pope Vigilius was in the city but refused to attend. He was put under heavy pressure and later accepted the decisions. The council did not win over the Miaphysites, and in the west it caused a new rift: churches in northern Italy broke with Rome for decades in protest. A later Third Council of Constantinople dealt with the next quarrel over Christ's nature.
sum: The fifth ecumenical council of the church, called by Justinian and held in Constantinople from May to June 553. Almost all the bishops were from the east.
